append.text: **Ps 99:2a *servíte Dómino in lætítia* → *sede servos do Senhor com alegria*** — D18 followed, in the verse D18 named (*Aclamai* sounds first in the same verse). The Latinist (v1 and v2 gate, minor) and the stylist asked *servi ao Senhor* again; held, option 2. The ambiguity reader noted *sede* may flash as 'thirst' before the imperative is heard.

**Ps 99:3b *introíte portas ejus in confessióne … confitémini illi* → *entrai com ação de graças pelas suas portas … dai-lhe graças*** — noun and verb one family, as the row foresaw (= 94:2). The v1 stylist heard *graças / graças* chime at mediant and final: the manner phrase moved first (order only), so the echo stays off the mediant. The v2 Latinist (minor) asked *louvor … louvai-o*, calling it defensible; held, option.
**Ps 99:3b *oves páscuæ ejus* → *as ovelhas da sua pastagem*** — the row; the stylist asked *pasto* (plainer), refused for the row (73:1, 78:13, 94:7), option.
Ps 99:4b *quóniam suávis est Dóminus* → *porque o Senhor é suave* — the row; the ambiguity reader heard 'gentle, kind', with a risk of colloquial 'chill'.
Ps 99:3b *átria ejus in hymnis* → *com hinos nos seus átrios* (the elided *introíte*; 95:8's *nos*); unknown to the ambiguity reader again; kept.
**Ps 99:2b *Introíte in conspéctu ejus* → *Entrai na sua presença*** — a verb of motion, as 118:170; no reader remarked.
Ps 99:2a *Jubiláte Deo, omnis terra* → *Aclamai a Deus, toda a terra* (= 65:1); no remark.
Ps 99:2b *in exsultatióne* → *com exultação*; the psalm's four *in* of manner all *com* (99:2a *com alegria*); *exultação* unknown to the ambiguity reader again; kept.

**Ps 99:4b *et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas ejus* → *e de geração em geração a sua verdade*** — the only place with *usque* (grep); absorbed, as MS1932. The v1 Latinist (minor) asked *até geração e geração*, refused as not Portuguese, option.

terms: | ipse … ipsi (contrast of agents: *ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos*) | ele mesmo … nós mesmos (*ele mesmo nos fez, e não nós mesmos*) | open | Ps 99:3a; = 94:5 *ipse fecit illud* → *ele mesmo o fez* (same two Latin words, same Portuguese). The resumptive *Dóminus ipse est Deus* → *o Senhor, ele é Deus* (DRB 'the Lord he is God'; MS1932 drops ipse — option). The ambiguity reader heard 'we did not make ourselves' after a moment; the Latinist passed it twice. |
